name: Pololu DRV8825 Stepper Driver Carrier

summary: Pololu carrier for the TI DRV8825 bipolar stepper driver: STEP/DIR control, up to 1/32 microstepping, 8.2-45 V motor supply, no separate logic supply. Pin-compatible with the A4988 carrier in most systems.

warnings.text: Connecting or disconnecting a stepper motor while the driver is powered can destroy the driver (Pololu).

The carrier uses low-ESR ceramic capacitors, so LC voltage spikes on long power leads can exceed the DRV8825's 45 V rating even with a 12 V supply. Pololu recommends a large (at least 47 uF) electrolytic capacitor across VMOT and GND close to the board.

RST and SLP are pulled low inside the DRV8825 (RESET about 100k, SLEEP 1M), which keeps the driver off. Both must be driven high (2.2-5.25 V) for the driver to run. Unlike the A4988 carrier, SLEEP has no pull-up of its own; it only gets a 10k pull-up through FLT when FLT is tied to a logic supply.
The board can get hot enough to burn you long before the chip overheats (Pololu). Above about 1.5 A per coil it needs a heat sink or other cooling.

Microstep table (DRV8825 datasheet Table 1; M2/M1/M0): 0/0/0 = full step (71% current), 0/0/1 = 1/2, 0/1/0 = 1/4, 0/1/1 = 1/8, 1/0/0 = 1/16, 1/0/1, 1/1/0 and 1/1/1 = 1/32. M0-M2 have internal 100k pull-downs, so leaving them unconnected gives full step. Note: the all-high setting that gives 1/16 on the A4988 gives 1/32 here.

Timing (DRV8825 datasheet 7.6): STEP high and STEP low at least 1.9 us each, STEP frequency at most 250 kHz, DIR/MODE setup and hold 650 ns around the STEP rising edge, nENBL active to STEP 650 ns, wake-up time from SLEEP high to STEP accepted 1.7 ms max. These are slower than the A4988 (1 us pulses).

Voltages (DRV8825 datasheet): motor supply VM 8.2-45 V. There is no logic supply pin: the chip makes its own 3.3 V (V3P3OUT, 3.2-3.4 V). Logic inputs read high from 2.2 V to 5.25 V and low up to 0.7 V, so 3.3 V and 5 V controllers both work. 3.3 V is shown as the logic voltage because it is the internal logic level.

FLT sits where the A4988 carrier has VDD. The DRV8825's nFAULT is open drain and goes low on overcurrent or overtemperature shutdown. Pololu adds a 1.5k series resistor so it is safe to connect FLT straight to a logic supply, and a 10k resistor from FLT to SLP (pull-up for FAULT when SLEEP is held high, or pull-up for SLEEP when FLT is tied to logic power). The 10k resistor is absent on the first (md20a) board version.
Current limit (Pololu): Current limit = VREF x 2 (0.100 ohm sense resistors), e.g. VREF 0.5 V for 1 A.

pins.label: EN
pins.notes: Active low. High turns the outputs off (high impedance) and STEP is ignored; low enables. Internal ~100k pull-down, so the driver is enabled when this pin is left unconnected.

pins.label: M0
pins.notes: Microstep select bit 0. Internal 100k pull-down. See the microstep table in the board warnings.

pins.label: RST
pins.notes: Active low. Low resets the indexer to home and disables the outputs; STEP is ignored. Internal ~100k pull-down, so it must be driven high for the driver to run. Also clears a latched overcurrent fault.

pins.label: SLP
pins.notes: Active low. Low = sleep (outputs, charge pump and 3.3 V regulator off; all inputs ignored). Internal 1M pull-down, so it must be driven high. On the carrier it connects to FLT through 10k. Wait up to 1.7 ms after waking before STEP. Any external pull-up should be 4.7k or less so a fault can't pull SLEEP low.

pins.label: STEP
pins.notes: Each rising edge moves the indexer one step. Minimum high and low pulse width 1.9 us, max 250 kHz. Internal 100k pull-down.

pins.label: DIR
pins.notes: Direction. 650 ns setup and hold around the STEP rising edge. Internal 100k pull-down, so it can be left unconnected for one direction.

pins.label: VMOT
pins.notes: Motor supply, 8.2-45 V. Undervoltage lockout disables the chip until VM rises above the UVLO threshold (7.8 V typical, 8.2 V max, rising). Add a 47 uF or larger electrolytic close to the board.

pins.label: B2
pins.notes: Coil B output (same position and function as 2B on the A4988 carrier). Never connect or disconnect the motor while powered.

pins.label: FLT
pins.notes: Open-drain fault output through a 1.5k series resistor; low on overcurrent (latched until RESET or power cycle) or overtemperature (clears automatically when cooled). Pulled up through 10k to SLP. Safe to wire to a logic supply, as in A4988 sockets where this is VDD.
